chapter: Later ventures, lodges and San Francisco recollections
title: Edna Hightower, pianist in Kansas City and Los Angeles
summary: Willard asks about Alma Hightower; Spikes recalls Edna Hightower as pianist in the Kansas City show around 1910 who later led the Hightowers Orchestra in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: How about a lady named Alma Hightower?

Well, Edna Hightower--I told you--when we went to Kansas City to play in that theater, she was the piano player there. This is 19 and, uh, oh, '9 or '10. She was the piano player, and the other people were men. Then, after she came home...she came here in
about '18 or '19 or something like that, and she played around here for a long time till she got too old to play...
Well, did she lead a band? I heard that she taught a lot of people but...
Yeah, she did, after she come here, she taught here, but she was playing back there.
Did she ever lead a band here in Los Angeles? Or play in a band here?
I think she had a band called The Hightowers Orchestra.
Was it all girls, or was it...
I understand that she was a very good musician.
She...I guess she was. I don't know about her ability. I know she played...
But there were some all-girl bands working here in Los Angeles...
Well, my brother had one, and I...I, uh...I think ...I think she had one for awhile. I don't know for sure.
